meta_description: A native Mac password manager for Vaultwarden and Bitwarden. All features are free for personal use. A one-time license costs {price}; required for work use.
meta_title: Triwarden — the native Mac password manager for Vaultwarden & Bitwarden
meta_og_image_alt: The Triwarden app icon, a three-ring dial around a keyhole
hero_lede: A native Mac password manager for Vaultwarden and Bitwarden. Unlock with Touch ID and find the login you need with a keyboard shortcut.
languages_label: Languages: English, Traditional Chinese (Taiwan), Traditional Chinese (Hong Kong), Simplified Chinese, Japanese
screens_lede: Built with SwiftUI, with light and dark themes, keyboard shortcuts and VoiceOver support.
alt_vault: The vault: sidebar, item list, and a GitHub login with its password, live one-time code, passkey and attachments
alt_codes: A grid of one-time codes, each with a countdown ring
alt_watchtower: Watchtower showing a security score, passwords found in breach data and reused passwords.
alt_palette: The command palette over the vault, searching “git”: GitHub first with its live code, then GitLab, Gitea and more
alt_generator: The generator with length, character sets and history
alt_menubar: The menu bar panel: the page’s login, favorites with live codes, quick actions and the generator
alt_signin: Signing in to a self-hosted Vaultwarden server
cap_vault: Logins, cards, notes, identities and SSH keys, organized with folders and favorites.
cap_codes: Every one-time code at a glance, each with its countdown ring. Click to copy.
cap_watchtower: Review security issues and open the affected site to update your password.
cap_palette: Find vault items and run Triwarden commands. ⌘K in the app, ⇧⌘Space from other apps.
cap_generator: Generate passwords, passphrases and usernames, and review recent results.
cap_menubar: The page you’re on, your favorites and their codes, one click from any app.
cap_signin: Self-hosted, Bitwarden US or Bitwarden EU — pick one and sign in.
cap_lock: The lock: a vault door that turns as you type, and takes itself apart when you’re in.
palette_p1: Press {shortcut} in another app to find a login. Triwarden can prioritize matches for the current website or app. Select an item to type its username and password; Auto-Type requires macOS Accessibility permission.
palette_p2: In Triwarden, press {shortcut} to search items and run commands such as New Login or Lock Vault.
row_menubar_body: The login for the page you’re on, your favorites with live codes, quick actions and the generator — all in the menu bar.
row_ssh_title: Your SSH keys, guarded by Touch ID.
row_ssh_body: Store SSH keys in your vault and connect {ssh} to Triwarden. Approve authentication and Git signing with Touch ID or your Mac password. See the guide for {path} setup.
row_cli_title: Use commands and shortcuts with your vault.
row_cli_body: Use {tw} in scripts, Shortcuts and App Intents. Safari and Chrome integrations connect your browser to the vault. Requests to read secrets require approval with Touch ID or your Mac password.
security_lede: Vault data is encrypted on your Mac before syncing. Use your master password, Touch ID or PIN to unlock, and choose self-hosted Vaultwarden or Bitwarden cloud for storage.
lock1_body: Your master password is used locally to derive keys with PBKDF2 or Argon2id. Vault contents are encrypted before they are sent to your server.
lock2_body: On supported Macs, Touch ID uses Secure Enclave protection for saved unlock keys. Master password and PIN unlock are also available.
lock3_body: Connect to self-hosted Vaultwarden or Bitwarden cloud in the US or EU. Sync encrypted vault data, receive live updates when the server supports them, and read cached items offline.
lock4_title: A little detail in every unlock.
lock4_body: On the lock screen the rings turn as you type. When the last one lands in line, the door takes itself apart.
gen_body: Generate passwords, passphrases from the EFF wordlist, and usernames. Recent results are saved in the generator history.
wt_p1: Find breached, reused or weak passwords, insecure website addresses, and sites that may support two-step login. Open the site to review or change your settings.
wt_p2: Breach checks use Have I Been Pwned’s k-anonymity: five characters of a hash leave your Mac, never the password.
more_autofill_b: Fill passwords, passkeys and one-time codes where the browser or app supports macOS AutoFill. Enable Triwarden as a provider in System Settings.
more_send_b: Share text or a file through an encrypted link. Edit it later; the link stays the same.
more_emergency_b: On servers that support emergency access, invite a trusted contact and choose a waiting period for access to your vault.
more_import_b: 1Password, LastPass, KeePass, Bitwarden, Proton Pass, Dashlane, Apple Passwords, Chrome, Firefox.
more_accounts_b: Self-hosted and cloud side by side. One Touch ID unlocks them all.
more_orgs_b: Shared vaults with nested shared folders. Show one vault, several or all of them; event logs for admins.
more_offline_b: Unlock and read previously synced items from the encrypted local cache. Syncing and server features need a connection.
more_clipboard_b: Copied secrets clear themselves, with a countdown in the footer.
more_history_b: View edit dates and the previous passwords retained with an item.
more_bulk_b: ⌘-click, ⇧-click or ⌘A, then move, archive or trash them in one go.
more_2fa_b: Authenticator app, email, recovery codes, and approving sign-ins from your other devices.
more_lang_b: English, 繁體中文 (台灣 · 香港), 简体中文 and 日本語.
more_unlock_b: One touch unlocks every account; a lock timeout for each, or log out instead of lock.
more_a11y_b: VoiceOver, full keyboard control, Increase Contrast and Reduce Motion.
price_lede: Personal use is free. Using Triwarden for work requires a paid license. All features remain available without a time limit. Buying a license supports development and removes purchase reminders.
tier_free_body: All features, with no time limit for personal use. After 30 days, the app may show a purchase reminder at most once a week.
tier_license_body: Support development, remove purchase reminders and receive future updates. The license covers one person on all their Macs, including a company Mac.
tier_license_note: Personal use is free. Using Triwarden for work requires a paid license. One license covers your personal and work use on all your Macs. Each team member needs their own license.
price_reminder: Purchase reminders start after 30 days, at most once a week. Features remain available, and installing an update does not add a reminder.
price_faq1_q: Is this a subscription or a one-time fee?
price_faq1_a: The license costs {price} as a one-time payment and includes future updates. There is no subscription or renewal fee.
price_faq2_q: How many Macs does one license cover?
price_faq2_a: One license covers one person on all the Macs they use, including a company Mac, with no device limit. Each additional user needs a separate license.
price_faq3_q: How do I pay and activate?
price_faq3_a: Purchase through Lemon Squeezy. After payment, find your license key in the confirmation email and paste it into Triwarden › Settings › License. Available payment methods and any applicable taxes are shown at checkout.
price_faq4_q: Can my company buy a license for me?
price_faq4_a: Yes. A company can buy a license and assign it to one named person, who can use it on personal or company Macs. Each user needs a separate license.
honest1_b: Personal use has no time limit. Buying a license supports development and removes purchase reminders.
honest2_b: Purchased keys are activated with Lemon Squeezy when you register them on a Mac. The saved license is then read locally, without recurring checks.
honest3_b: The source is available under GPL-3.0. You can build it yourself; paid-key terms do not limit your GPL rights.
faq1_q: Is anything locked until I pay?
faq1_a: No features are locked. Personal use is free with no time limit. After 30 days, a purchase reminder may appear at most once a week. Work or business use requires a license.
faq2_q: How many Macs does one license cover?
faq2_a: One license costs {price} once and covers one person on all their Macs, including a company Mac. It has no expiry and includes future updates. Resale, transfer and sharing between users are not allowed.
faq3_q: When does Triwarden connect to other services?
faq3_a: Triwarden connects to your vault server to sign in and sync. License activation uses Lemon Squeezy; enabled update checks use GitHub. Watchtower can query password-breach and two-step-login services. See Privacy for details.
faq4_q: Which servers does it work with?
faq4_a: Self-hosted Vaultwarden and Bitwarden cloud in the US and EU. You can use several accounts together. Some features depend on your server version, plan and permissions.
faq5_q: Can I build it from source?
faq5_a: Yes. Triwarden is free software under the GPL-3.0; building it yourself is always free. Forks need their own name and icon.
faq6_q: What if I use Triwarden for both personal and work accounts?
faq6_a: Personal use is free. Using Triwarden for work requires a paid license. Work accounts include company email, company GitHub, client systems and accounts used for freelance work. One license covers your personal and work use on all your Macs. Each team member needs their own license. The purpose of use decides whether a license is needed, not who owns the Mac.
faq7_q: Can I share or resell my license?
faq7_a: No. A paid license key is assigned to one person. It cannot be resold, transferred, lent or shared with other users. See License terms for details.
close_body: Use every feature free for personal use. A one-time license costs {price}, supports development and removes purchase reminders. Required for work use.
close_requires: Requires macOS 26 or later. Update checks are optional; Homebrew users can update with brew upgrade.
purchase_meta_description: Personal use is free with all features. A one-time license costs {price}, covers one person on unlimited Macs, and is required for work use.
purchase_h1: Personal use is free. Licenses are one-time.
purchase_lede: Buy a license for {price} to support development and remove purchase reminders. One person, unlimited Macs, future updates included. Personal use can stay free; work use requires a license.
privacy_meta_description: How Triwarden handles vault data, local storage, license activation, updates and optional network services, and how this website loads fonts and release information.
privacy_lede: Triwarden is a client for your Vaultwarden or Bitwarden account. We don’t host your passwords, and the app doesn’t run ad tracking.
privacy_s1_b: Logins, notes, keys and attachments sync with your chosen Vaultwarden or Bitwarden server. Triwarden encrypts and decrypts vault contents on your Mac. Triwarden does not host your vault.
privacy_s2_t: What the app stores on your Mac
privacy_s2_b: An encrypted local cache, Keychain items for unlock, sessions and (if you register) your license, plus settings in standard macOS preferences. That keeps the app working offline and with Touch ID — not for analytics.
privacy_s3_b:
When you activate a purchased license key on a Mac, Triwarden sends the key and a random installation identifier to Lemon Squeezy. After successful activation, it stores the license locally without recurring license checks. Registering the key again, including on another Mac, makes another activation request. Offline-format keys are verified locally.

Payments are processed by Lemon Squeezy under its Privacy Policy.
privacy_s4_b: When updates are enabled, Sparkle may check GitHub for a newer build. That request does not include vault data. GitHub’s own policy: GitHub Privacy Statement.
privacy_s5_b: The marketing site is static. It may fetch public GitHub star and release metadata (for download size). It loads webfonts from Google Fonts (Google Privacy Policy). Your light/dark theme choice is stored in the browser’s localStorage only. We don’t run advertising or third-party tracking pixels on these pages.
privacy_s6_b:
Depending on what you use:

  • Lemon Squeezy Privacy — checkout and receipt-key activation
  • GitHub Privacy Statement — releases, stars, Sparkle update checks
  • Google Privacy Policy — fonts on this website
  • Pwned Passwords
  • 2FA Directory
terms_meta_description: Paid License terms ({price}): one person, all their Macs; work use; GPL source remains free. Not for resale or team sharing.
terms_lede: These terms describe paid license keys for official Triwarden builds. The source code is licensed separately under GPL-3.0, and these terms do not limit those rights.
terms_note: There is no device activation limit. Resale, sharing a key publicly, or sharing it between users may lead to revocation. For refunds, contact support; requests follow the payment provider’s process and applicable purchase terms.
terms_s1_b:
A paid license is assigned to one person.

  • That person can activate it on all the Macs they use, including a company Mac, with no device limit.
  • The key cannot be resold, transferred, lent or shared with other users.

For multiple users, each needs a separate license. A company may purchase licenses and assign each to one named person.
terms_s2_b:
Personal use is free. Using Triwarden for work requires a paid license.

Work accounts include company email, company GitHub, client systems and accounts used for freelance work.

One license covers your personal and work use on all your Macs. Each team member needs their own license.

The purpose of use decides whether a license is needed, not who owns the Mac. Managing only personal accounts remains free on a company Mac. Managing work accounts requires a license even on your own Mac.

Personal use, including home self-hosted Vaultwarden, can remain free. After 30 days, the app may show a purchase reminder at most once a week. No features are locked.
terms_s3_b:
A paid key removes the official build’s purchase reminders and covers work use under these terms. It does not replace or limit the source code’s GPL-3.0 license.

You can build the source yourself under the GPL without purchasing a key. These paid-key terms do not limit those GPL rights. Forks must use their own name and icon.
terms_s4_b: For purchase, product or privacy questions, email {email}.
terms_s5_b: Updated terms may apply to new purchases. Existing licenses keep the rights stated at purchase, except where misuse leads to revocation.
foot_disclaimer: Not affiliated with Bitwarden, Inc. or the Vaultwarden project. Bitwarden is a trademark of Bitwarden, Inc.
row_autotype_body: Use the palette to choose a login and type its username and password into the focused app. Or press {shortcut} for direct Auto-Type. Requires macOS Accessibility permission; results depend on the target app’s fields.
kt_submit: Add to any of these to submit too
kt_global: From anywhere: fill the page or app you’re in
alt_search: Searching “north” across My vault and the Northwind shared vault, with filter chips under the field
cap_search: One search over every vault, with filters that stay on between launches.
search_body: Search personal and shared vaults, then narrow the results with {tokens} or the filter menu. Active filters appear below the search field and are saved between launches.
speed_note: Download size of the latest release. Memory measured with make bench on an Apple M4 Pro with a 200+ item vault; it varies by Mac.
more_keys_b: Help › Keyboard Shortcuts (⌘/) lists every key — in the window, the palette and system-wide.
g_meta: How to use Triwarden's SSH agent: keys in your vault for ssh and git, approved with Touch ID or your Mac password.
g_lede: Triwarden acts as an SSH agent for ssh and git, using SSH Key items in your vault. Signing happens inside the app; clients receive the signature, not the private key. Approval frequency is configurable.
g_flow_caption: ssh requests a signature. Triwarden checks approval, prompts with Touch ID or your Mac password when needed, and returns the signature.
g_s1_b: Open Triwarden › Settings › Developer and switch on Use Triwarden as SSH agent. It runs while the app is open and offers keys only while your vault is unlocked.
g_s2_b: Make a new SSH Key item. Press Generate Ed25519 Key for a fresh one, or paste a private key you already have — an unencrypted OpenSSH key (-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----). Ed25519, ECDSA (P-256, P-384, P-521) and RSA all work, and SSH keys saved by other Bitwarden apps show up too.
g_s2_tip: Key has a passphrase? The agent can’t use encrypted keys. Make an unencrypted copy, paste it into the item, then delete the copy — the vault keeps it encrypted from then on.
g_s3_b: Add the agent to ~/.ssh/config — Settings › Developer › SSH setup has a Copy button with your own path filled in. Or set it for a single shell.
g_s3_note: Prefer the config file: apps opened from the Dock (VS Code, Tower, Fork, Xcode) don’t see your shell’s variables, but every ssh reads the config.
g_s4_b: ssh-add -L lists the public keys the agent offers. Nothing there? See the fixes below.
g_c1_b: Copy the item’s public key into GitHub › Settings › SSH and GPG keys as an Authentication key (GitLab: User settings › SSH keys). Then test it:
g_c2_b: Add the public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the server, then connect with ssh. Triwarden’s agent returns signatures without sending your private key to ssh.
g_c3_b: On the key’s page, Git signing › Copy Setup gives you these three lines. Add the same public key to GitHub as a Signing key and your commits show Verified.
g_c3_note: To check signatures locally too, list the keys you trust:
g_c4_b: With many keys, a server can stop at “Too many authentication failures” before it reaches the right one. Save that key’s public half to a file and pin it to the host:
g_c5_b: Rather keep another agent for everything else? Use Triwarden for named hosts only:
g_c6_b: VS Code, Tower, Fork, Xcode and anything else that runs the system’s ssh pick up ~/.ssh/config, so they work once step 3 is done. The approval appears for them the same way.
g_appr_b: Each request names the program and the key — “allow ssh to sign with the SSH key GitHub”. Choose how often to be asked in Settings › Developer › Ask before signing:
g_appr_o1_b: the default: one prompt per signature
g_appr_o2_b: handy for a burst of git fetches
g_appr_o3_b: for long sessions; locking forgets it
g_appr_nomac: If Touch ID is unavailable, macOS can ask for your Mac password. Choose Deny to reject a request. Settings › Developer lists recent approvals and denials.
g_sec_1: The agent signs inside Triwarden; ssh and git receive signatures, not the private key.
g_sec_2: Locked vault, no keys: the agent offers nothing until you unlock, and locking forgets every remembered approval.
g_sec_3: Archived and deleted items are never offered.
g_tr1_a: The vault is locked, the agent is off, there are no SSH Key items, or the key in the item has a passphrase (encrypted keys aren’t offered).
g_tr2_q: “Could not open a connection to your authentication agent”
g_tr2_a: This shell doesn’t know where the agent is. Add the IdentityAgent line to ~/.ssh/config, or run the export from step 3 in that shell.
g_tr3_a: The request was denied, or the prompt was left until it timed out. Run the command again and approve.
g_tr4_a: The server gave up before reaching the right key. Pin the key to the host (Several keys, above).
g_cta_b: The SSH agent is included in free personal use. Work use requires a license.
price_scope: The purpose of use decides whether a license is needed, not who owns the Mac. One license covers your personal and work use on all your Macs. Each team member needs their own license.
price_faq5_q: Can I share a license with my team?
price_faq5_a: No. Each person needs a separate license; a company may purchase and assign one to each user. A shared team key is not supported.
home_price_lede: Personal use includes every feature with no time limit. A license supports development and removes purchase reminders. Work or business use requires a license.
home_price_scope: Personal use is free. Using Triwarden for work requires a paid license. One license covers your personal and work use on all your Macs. Each team member needs their own license.
privacy_s7_b: For purchase, product or privacy questions, email {email}.
how1_b: Get the signed app from GitHub, or install it with Homebrew.
how2_b: All features are available with no time limit for personal use. Work use requires a license.
how3_b: Pay {price} through Lemon Squeezy, then paste the emailed key into Settings › License.
how4_b: Your license has no expiry and includes future updates. There is no renewal fee.
faq8_a: Email {email} for purchase or product questions. Report bugs through GitHub Issues. For security reports, follow the Security policy.
privacy_s8_b:
Password-breach checks contact Have I Been Pwned’s Pwned Passwords service with the first five characters of a SHA-1 password hash, not the password or its full hash. Two-step-login information can be downloaded from 2FA Directory. Opening a change-password link may query the saved site to locate its password-change page.

When website icons are enabled, requested domain names are sent to your account’s configured icon service (Vaultwarden or Bitwarden). These requests do not include item passwords.
hero_purchase_note: Free for personal use · One-time license {price} · Required for work use.
price_faq6_q: Do I need a license for personal accounts on my own Mac?
price_faq6_a: No. Managing only personal or household accounts, including a home Vaultwarden server, is free with every feature.
price_faq7_q: What if I use Triwarden for both personal and work accounts?
price_faq7_a: Yes. Managing any work accounts requires one paid license. It also covers your personal use on all your Macs; you do not need separate personal and work licenses.
price_faq8_q: Do I need a license just because I use a company Mac?
price_faq8_a: No. Managing only personal accounts remains free on a company Mac. Managing work accounts requires a license even on your own Mac.
